title: monotonic-traffic-annealer-with-explainable-failover
author: Maya Singh
ci_status: pass (two flaky integration runs, rerun fixed)
description:
Context: We need a safer, explainable way to move traffic between model variants for multi-stage rollouts (canary -> ramp -> steady) while bounding user exposure and providing a deterministic automated rollback path. This PR introduces the "monotonic traffic annealer", a scheduler that incrementally increases traffic in a strictly monotonic schedule with per-cohort exposure throttles and an explainability hook that attaches decision metadata to each traffic transition.
Motivation: existing gradual-swap controllers allow non-monotonic jumps during emergency rollbacks or manual adjustments which led to two incidents last quarter where small numeric regressions were amplified by oscillatory traffic.
Design summary:
- Monotonic annealing: traffic percentage only increases during normal progress; decreases are only allowed via an explicit rollback workflow (automated or operator-triggered).
- Exposure throttles: per-cohort limits that cap absolute user-exposure (requests/hour) rather than percentage only. This prevents large cohorts from being overwhelmed during fast ramps.
- Explainability hooks: every transition emits a DecisionTrace (policy id, metric anchors, chosen step, confidence score, evaluated constraints) as structured tracing tags and a compact JSON blob in rollout telemetry.
- Failover semantics: when safety gates fail, the annealer transitions into a "quarantine" hold state and triggers the rollback playbook (pre-defined sequential steps: snapshot -> scale-back-to-stable -> run-replay). Rollback playbook is implemented as automatable recipes that can be bound to Linear/Jira tickets or executed manually from Console.
Compatibility:
- Backwards compatible with existing rollout CRD; new fields are optional (annealSchedule, exposureThrottle, explainabilityEnabled).
- When disabled, controller behavior is identical to previous staged-swap.
Operator UX:
- Console exposes an "Anneal preview" view showing simulated exposure curves for selected cohorts and a human-readable rationale for each step.
- CLI: redwood rollout plan --simulate --cohort <id> prints a step-by-step plan and DecisionTrace summaries.
Observability & telemetry:
- New metrics: rollout_anneal_step{cohort,policy}, rollout_exposure_violation_count, rollout_decision_confidence (histogram).
- Traces include decision.trace_id and decision.reason.
- Logs include a compact JSON per-transition at INFO level for operators.
Safety & testing:
- Unit tests for schedule math and constraint evaluation.
- Integration tests simulate 3-cohort scenarios with synthetic latency regressions and verify automatic quarantine + rollback triggers.
- Load test: 50% higher steady-state throughput to validate throttles.
Rollout plan & migration:
- Default rollout mode remains unchanged. Admins must opt-in by setting rolloutMode: "anneal" or via Console toggle.
- Migration path for active rollouts: controller detects legacy rollouts and refuses to adopt them unless annotated migrate=true; this prevents mid-rollover behavior ambiguity.
Checklist:
- [x] Core annealer algorithm implemented and unit tested
- [x] DecisionTrace schema and telemetry hooks
- [x] Console preview and CLI simulate implemented
- [x] Integration + e2e tests added
- [x] Docs and runbook drafted (link below)
- [x] Performance benchmark against staged-swap (no regressions observed within noise)
Related: design doc: https://linear.app/redwood/doc/monotonic-annealer and runbook: https://docs.redwood.ai/runbooks/rollout-annealer.
Migration Linear: ENG-8743.
Impact: This adds observable safety to rollouts and simplifies operator reasoning during incidents at the cost of a modest controller CPU increase (~2-4%) due to additional constraint evaluation.
Implementation notes:
- DecisionTrace is intentionally compact (max 1KB) to avoid tracing noise.
- Exposure throttles use token-bucket counters sharded per-cohort for scalability.
- Anneal schedule supports exponential, linear, and custom step arrays.
CI / Flaky runs: Integration job failed initially due to an async test asserting on telemetry ordering; test was made more robust and CI passed on rerun.
Merge notes: squashed four commits into one for clarity. See commits below for granular history.

review_comments: Diego Torres: Nice work — algorithm looks clean. Two quick asks: (1) can we make the exposureThrottle units configurable (reqs/min vs reqs/hr) and (2) consider adding a metric for 'time-in-quarantine' to help post-mortems.
Maya Singh (author): Response: made units configurable via exposureThrottle.unit and added rollout_quarantine_duration_seconds metric as a histogram. Updated tests accordingly.
Laura Bennett: We should ensure DecisionTrace doesn't leak PII. Please confirm fields are schema-validated and sanitized before emission.
Maya Singh (author): Confirmed. DecisionTrace undergoes schema validation and a scrub step; sensitive fields are redacted. Added unit test for sanitizer.
Evan Park: Integration test looks heavy — can we add a lighter smoke test that asserts the monotonic property only?
Maya Singh (author): Added smoke tests (tests/unit/anneal_monotonic_smoke_test.go) and moved heavier scenario to e2e tag.
review_summary: Maintainer merge: Maya squashed and merged (2026-01-22)
release_notes: Introduce monotonic traffic annealer: adds controlled monotonic ramping, per-cohort exposure throttles, explainable DecisionTraces, and automated rollback playbook. Opt-in while backward compatible. See docs for migration steps.
notes: Operators: opt-in via rolloutMode: "anneal" or enable in Console under Settings > Rollouts.
Rollback playbook is idempotent; however, when binding to Linear/Jira it will attach the snapshot id to the ticket automatically.
Performance: expect 2-4% additional CPU on controller; memory impact negligible.
